normality_check_outcome_score.plain_english: Shapiro-Wilk test on primary outcome score (W=0.995, p=0.100): data appears normally distributed — a t-test/ANOVA is appropriate.

primary_endpoint_ttest.plain_english: On average, the Drug X arm scored 7.90 points higher than Placebo on primary outcome score (0-100) (60.05 vs 52.15). This difference is statistically significant (Welch's t=7.98, p=< 0.001), meaning we would see a difference this large by chance in fewer than 0.1% of repeated trials. The effect size is medium (Cohen's d = 0.71).

ci_outcome_drug_x.plain_english: The 95% confidence interval for Drug X primary outcome score is [58.51, 61.60] around a sample mean of 60.05 (n=250).

ci_outcome_placebo.plain_english: The 95% confidence interval for Placebo primary outcome score is [50.96, 53.34] around a sample mean of 52.15 (n=250).

hba1c_control_chisq.plain_english: A chi-square test of independence was run on HbA1c <7% control at Week 24 across treatment arms (chi2=56.11, dof=1, p=< 0.001). There is a statistically significant association between treatment arm and HbA1c <7% control at Week 24.

ae_occurrence_chisq.plain_english: A chi-square test of independence was run on adverse event occurrence across treatment arms (chi2=43.35, dof=1, p=< 0.001). There is a statistically significant association between treatment arm and adverse event occurrence.

ae_severity_class_chisq.plain_english: A chi-square test of independence was run on adverse event severity class across treatment arms (chi2=49.90, dof=2, p=< 0.001). There is a statistically significant association between treatment arm and adverse event severity class.

kruskal_hba1c_by_ae_class.plain_english: A Kruskal-Wallis test compared HbA1c reduction by Week 24, grouped by worst AE severity across 3 groups without assuming normally distributed data (H=35.41, p=< 0.001). The groups differ significantly in HbA1c reduction by Week 24, grouped by worst AE severity. Median values: No AE=0.32, Mild AE=0.67, Severe AE=0.44.
